variables.name: STUDYID
variables.label: Study Identifier
variables.description: Unique identifier for a study.

variables.name: DOMAIN
variables.label: Domain Abbreviation
variables.description: Two-character abbreviation for the domain.

variables.name: USUBJID
variables.label: Unique Subject Identifier
variables.description: Identifier used to uniquely identify a subject across all studies for all applications or submissions involving the product.

variables.name: CPSEQ
variables.label: Sequence Number
variables.description: Sequence number to ensure uniqueness of subject records within a domain. May be any valid number.

variables.name: CPGRPID
variables.label: Group ID
variables.description: Used to tie together a block of related records in a single domain for a subject.

variables.name: CPREFID
variables.label: Reference ID
variables.description: Internal or external specimen identifier.

variables.name: CPSPID
variables.label: Sponsor-Defined Identifier
variables.description: Sponsor-defined reference number. May be preprinted on the CRF as an explicit line identifier or defined in the sponsor's operational database. Example: Line number on the lab page.

variables.name: CPLNKID
variables.label: Link ID
variables.description: Identifier used to link related records across domains. This may be a one-to-one or a one-to-many relationship.

variables.name: CPLNKGRP
variables.label: Link Group ID
variables.description: Identifier used to link related records across domains. This will usually be a many-to-one relationship.

variables.name: CPTESTCD
variables.label: Test or Examination Short Name
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C181173
variables.description: Short name of the measurement, test, or examination described in CPTEST. It can be used as a column name when converting a dataset from a vertical to a horizontal format. The value in CPTESTCD cannot be longer than 8 characters, nor can it start with a number (e.g., "1TEST" is not valid). CPTESTCD cannot contain characters other than letters, numbers, or underscores. Examples: "MONO", "MNS".

variables.name: CPTEST
variables.label: Name of Measurement, Test or Examination
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C181174
variables.description: Long name for CPTESTCD. For cell phenotyping, the name (often abbreviated) of the cell population, as it is generally accepted by the scientific community, is populated (rather than a colloquial designation based on a primary marker, e.g., TLym Help rather than CD4). When the test is for a sublineage which can only be identified by specifying additional markers (i.e., has not been given a name) or which is further restricted to a subpopulation based on a particular cell state (e.g., activated, proliferating, apoptotic), the Sublineage Marker String (CPSBMRKS), Cell State (CPCELSTA), and Cell State Marker String (CPCSMRKS) variables are additionally populated and the value in CPTEST is suffixed with "Sub" to denote that it is a subset of the population identified in CPTEST (e.g., Monocytes Sub). \n The value in CPTEST cannot be longer than 40 characters.

variables.name: CPSBMRKS
variables.label: Sublineage Marker String
variables.description: Used to further subset the cell population identified in CPTEST based on the use of additional marker(s) that define a sublineage. The value in CPSBMRKS is used in combination with values in CPTEST and CPCELSTA to fully describe the cell population being measured. As such, it is an essential component of the full test name. \n For example, three unnamed sublineages of monocytes have been identified as: CCR2+CD16-, CCR2-CD16+, and CCR2+CD16+. Whereas the entire monocyte cell population can be defined as CD14+ cells, the additional CCR2 and CD16 markers are used to differentiate one sublineage from another. As none of these sublineages have been given names, they are only known by the CCR2 and CD16 marker combinations. By associating the CPTEST value of "Monocytes Sub" with, for example, a value of "CCR2+CD16-" in CPSBMRKS, the full test is defined to be the CCR2+CD16- monocyte subpopulation.

variables.name: CPCELSTA
variables.label: Cell State
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C181172
variables.description: A textual description of a subset of the cell population identified in CPTEST based on a particular functional and/or biological state (e.g., "ACTIVATED", "PROLIFERATING", "SENESCENT"). When populated, the values in CPCELSTA and CPSMRKS, in combination with the values in CPTEST and CPSBMRKS, fully describe the cell population being measured.

variables.name: CPCSMRKS
variables.label: Cell State Marker String
variables.description: Identifies the marker(s) or indicator(s) used to define the cell state (i.e., the value in CPCELSTA). \n For example, when Ki67 expression is used to determine that a cell population is in a proliferating state (i.e., CPCELSTA value="PROLIFERATING"), the value "Ki67+" in CPCSMRKS indicates that positive expression of Ki67 was used to define the population as proliferating. Similarly, a value of "Ki67-" in CPCSMRKS would indicate that lack of expression of Ki67 defined the "NON-PROLIFERATING" cell state in CPCELSTA. The CPCSMRKS value is useful for quickly determining which marker(s) were used to classify (i.e., operationally define) a cell population based on a functional/biological state.

variables.name: CPTSTCND
variables.label: Test Condition
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C181175
variables.description: Identifies any planned condition imposed by the assay system on the specimen at the time the test is performed. --TSTCND is generally used to distinguish between two or more records where the same assay is performed under varying (as opposed to fixed) conditions, usually for the purpose of making a comparison. For example, when the same assay (identified in --TEST) is performed under stimulated and non-stimulated conditions, the --TSTCND variable is used distinguish between the records.

variables.name: CPCNDAGT
variables.label: Test Condition Agent
variables.description: The textual description of the agent, if applicable, used to impose the condition identified in CPTSTCND. For example, records might be produced for the same assay run under stimulating (CPTSTCND value = "STIMULATED") conditions produced by different stimulating agents (e.g., phorbol myristate acetate, concanavalin A, PHA-P, TNF-alpha, Ionomycin, candida antigen).

variables.name: CPBDAGNT
variables.label: Binding Agent
variables.description: The textual description of the agent that is binding to the entity in the CPTEST variable. The CPBDAGNT variable is used to indicate that there is a binding relationship between the entities in the CPTEST and CPBDAGNT variables, regardless of direction. \n The binding agent may be, but is not limited to, a test article; a portion of a test article; a substance related to a test article; an endogenous molecule; an allergen; an infectious agent; or a reagent (e.g., primary antibody) that confers the binding specificity for the measurement defined in CPTEST when it is needed to uniquely identify the test.

variables.name: CPABCLID
variables.label: Antibody Clone Identifier
variables.description: Identifies the antibody clone (e.g., supplier-provided catalog name) used to confer specificity for the binding agent specified in CPBDAGNT.

variables.name: CPMRKSTR
variables.label: Marker String
variables.description: The text string identifying the full set of markers/indicators used by the laboratory to operationally define the complete test based on the combination of CPTEST, CPSBMRKS, and CPCELSTA. Because laboratories often use different markers/indicators to identify a cell population, the relationship between a named cell population in CPTEST (as combined with CPSBMRKS and CPCELSTA values) and the set of markers used to identify that population is many-to-one. To ensure nuances important for accurately interpreting the data are accounted for and which arise from the use of different sets of markers, it is necessary to operationally define the test in terms of the complete set of markers/indicators used to perform that test.

variables.name: CPGATE
variables.label: Gate
variables.description: The sponsor-defined name assigned to a gate. Gates are electronic (i.e., a device setting or software-defined) boundaries set by a user to virtually parse a specimen into discrete populations based on a set of defined characteristics (e.g., presence, absence, or intensity of expression of various markers; physical size; internal complexity or granularity). Gates are used to constrain data collection or analysis to a specific cell population or region of interest within the specimen.

variables.name: CPGATDEF
variables.label: Gate Definition
variables.description: The text string identifying the set of parameters and the order in which they are applied to define the gating strategy. In practice, a series of 2-dimensional sub-gates based on different cell characteristics (i.e., markers/indicators/physical properties) are most often combined until the cell population of interest is sufficiently resolved (i.e., electronically isolated) from other cell populations contained within the specimen. \n For complex analyses, differences in gating strategies can produce subtle differences in results obtained for a test. To ensure nuances important for accurately interpreting the data are accounted for and which arise from the use of different gating strategies, it is often necessary to qualify the test in terms of the gating strategy. For some purposes, however, and at the discretion of the sponsor, only the ultimate or penultimate gate is identified. When specifying the gating strategy in CPGATDEF, each sub-gate should be listed in the order it was applied and separated from the next sub-gate using the pipe/vertical line ("|") character.

variables.name: CPSPTSTD
variables.label: Sponsor Test Description
variables.description: Sponsor's description of a test. The variable is intended to contain highly structured test description metadata used by a sponsor to unambiguously define (label) a test. Such values generally reside in a sponsor/laboratory test metadata repository. CPSPTSTD is not intended for unstructured (spontaneous) free text. \n An example of appropriate usage is when it is necessary to include identifying information for a target cell population on which a test is conducted when the target population is not part of the test name, e.g., tests for quantitative expression of a particular marker on a specific cell population.

variables.name: CPCAT
variables.label: Category
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C181171
variables.description: Used to define a category of topic-variable values across subjects. Examples: "IMMUNOPHENOTYPING", "CELL FUNCTION", "TARGET ENGAGEMENT".

variables.name: CPSCAT
variables.label: Subcategory
variables.description: A further categorization of CPCAT.

variables.name: CPTSTPNL
variables.label: Test Panel
variables.description: Sponsor-defined textual description used to group tests run together as part of a test panel. Can be used with --GRPID to ensure that relationships between associated tests are accurately identified.

variables.name: CPORRES
variables.label: Result or Finding in Original Units
variables.description: Result of the measurement or finding as originally received or collected.

variables.name: CPORRESU
variables.label: Original Units
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C71620
variables.description: Original units in which the data were collected. The unit for CPORRES. Examples: "10^6/L", "%", "MESF".

variables.name: CPRESSCL
variables.label: Result Scale
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C177910
variables.description: Classifies the scale of the original result value with respect to whether the result is quantitative, ordinal, nominal, or narrative.

variables.name: CPRESTYP
variables.label: Result Type
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C179588
variables.description: Classifies the kind of result (i.e., property type) originally reported for the test. Examples: "NUMBER CONCENTRATION", "NUMBER FRACTION", "RATIO".

variables.name: CPCOLSRT
variables.label: Collected Summary Result Type
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C177908
variables.description: Used to indicate the type of collected summary result. This includes source summary results collected on a CRF or provided by an external vendor (e.g., central lab). If the summary result is derived using individual source data records, this summary result should be represented in ADaM. If a sponsor has both a collected summary result and a derived summary result, the collected summary result should be represented in SDTM and the derived summary result should be represented in ADaM.

variables.name: CPORNRLO
variables.label: Reference Range Lower Limit in Orig Unit
variables.description: Lower end of reference range for continuous measurement in original units. Should be populated only for continuous results.

variables.name: CPORNRHI
variables.label: Reference Range Upper Limit in Orig Unit
variables.description: Upper end of reference range for continuous measurement in original units. Should be populated only for continuous results.

variables.name: CPSTRESC
variables.label: Result or Finding in Standard Format
variables.description: Contains the result value for all findings, copied or derived from CPORRES in a standard format or in standard units. CPSTRESC should store all results or findings in character format; if results are numeric, they should also be stored in numeric format in CPSTRESN.

variables.name: CPSTRESN
variables.label: Numeric Result/Finding in Standard Units
variables.description: Used for continuous or numeric results or findings in standard format; copied in numeric format from CPSTRESC. CPSTRESN should store all numeric test results or findings.

variables.name: CPSTRESU
variables.label: Standard Units
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C71620
variables.description: Standardized unit used for CPSTRESC or CPSTRESN.

variables.name: CPSTNRLO
variables.label: Reference Range Lower Limit-Std Units
variables.description: Lower end of reference range for continuous measurements for CPSTRESC/CPSTRESN in standardized units. Should be populated only for continuous results.

variables.name: CPSTNRHI
variables.label: Reference Range Upper Limit-Std Units
variables.description: Upper end of reference range for continuous measurements in standardized units. Should be populated only for continuous results.

variables.name: CPNRIND
variables.label: Reference Range Indicator
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C78736
variables.description: Indicates where the value falls with respect to reference range defined by CPORNRLO and CPORNRHI, CPSTNRLO and CPSTNRHI, or by CPSTNRC. Examples: "NORMAL", "ABNORMAL", "HIGH", "LOW". Sponsors should specify in the study metadata (Comments column in the Define-XML document) whether CPNRIND refers to the original or standard reference ranges and results. CPNRIND should not be used to indicate clinical significance.

variables.name: CPSTAT
variables.label: Completion Status
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66789
variables.description: Used to indicate that the test was not performed or that it was attempted but did not generate a result. Should be null if a result exists in CPORRES.

variables.name: CPREASND
variables.label: Reason Not Done
variables.description: Describes why a test was not performed, e.g., "BROKEN EQUIPMENT", "SUBJECT REFUSED", "SPECIMEN LOST". Used in conjunction with CPSTAT when value is "NOT DONE".

variables.name: CPNAM
variables.label: Vendor Name
variables.description: The name or identifier of the laboratory that performed the test.

variables.name: CPLOINC
variables.label: LOINC Code
variables.description: Code for the test from the LOINC code system. The sponsor is expected to provide the dictionary name and version used to map the terms utilizing the Define-XML external codelist attributes.

variables.name: CPSPEC
variables.label: Specimen Type
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C78734
variables.description: Defines the type of specimen used for a measurement. Examples: "BLOOD", "BONE MARROW".

variables.name: CPSPCCND
variables.label: Specimen Condition
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C78733
variables.description: The physical state or quality of a specimen for an assessment. Example: "CLOTTED".

variables.name: CPMETHOD
variables.label: Method of Test or Examination
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C85492
variables.description: Method of the test or examination. Example: "FLOW CYTOMETRY".

variables.name: CPANMETH
variables.label: Analysis Method
variables.description: Analysis method applied to obtain a summarized result. Analysis method describes the method of secondary processing applied to a complex observation result.

variables.name: CPLOBXFL
variables.label: Last Observation Before Exposure Flag
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Operationally-derived indicator used to identify the last non-missing value prior to RFXSTDTC. The value should be "Y" or null.

variables.name: CPBLFL
variables.label: Baseline Flag
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Indicator used to identify a baseline value. The value should be "Y" or null.

variables.name: CPDRVFL
variables.label: Derived Flag
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Used to indicate a derived record. The value should be "Y" or null. Records that represent the average of other records, or do not come from the CRF, or are not as originally received or collected are examples of records that might be derived for the submission datasets. If CPDRVFL = "Y", then CPORRES may be null, with CPSTRESC and (if numeric) CPSTRESN having the derived value.

variables.name: CPCLSIG
variables.label: Clinically Significant, Collected
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C66742
variables.description: Used to indicate whether a collected observation is clinically significant based on judgement.

variables.name: VISITNUM
variables.label: Visit Number
variables.description: Clinical encounter number. Numeric version of VISIT, used for sorting.

variables.name: VISIT
variables.label: Visit Name
variables.description: Protocol-defined description of clinical encounter. May be used in addition to VISITNUM and/or VISITDY.

variables.name: VISITDY
variables.label: Planned Study Day of Visit
variables.description: Planned study day of the visit based upon RFSTDTC in Demographics. Should be an integer.

variables.name: TAETORD
variables.label: Planned Order of Element within Arm
variables.description: Number that gives the planned order of the element within the arm.

variables.name: EPOCH
variables.label: Epoch
variables.codelist: Version-agnostic anchor resource for codelist C99079
variables.description: Epoch associated with the start date/time of the observation, or the date/time of collection if start date/time is not collected.

variables.name: CPDTC
variables.label: Date/Time of Collection
variables.description: Date/time of specimen collection represented in ISO 8601 character format.

variables.name: CPDY
variables.label: Study Day of Visit/Collection/Exam
variables.description: Study day of specimen collection, measured in integer days. Algorithm for calculations must be relative to the sponsor-defined RFSTDTC value in Demographics.

variables.name: CPTPT
variables.label: Planned Time Point Name
variables.description: Text description of time when a specimen is to be taken, as defined in the protocol. This may be represented as an elapsed time relative to a fixed reference point (i.e., to the value in CPTPTREF). Example: "1 hour post".

variables.name: CPTPTNUM
variables.label: Planned Time Point Number
variables.description: Numerical version of CPTPT to aid in sorting. When CPTPT is represented as an elapsed time relative to a fixed reference point (i.e., to the value in CPTPTREF), the values in CPTPTNUM should be assigned in ascending order relative to the value in CPTPTREF. For example, records for time points where CPTPT = "5 minutes post", 1 hour post", and "4 hours post" could be represented in CPTPTNUM as "1", "2", and "3", which maintains the order between CPTPT and CPTPTNUM with respect to the fixed time point reference in CPTPTREF.

variables.name: CPELTM
variables.label: Planned Elapsed Time from Time Point Ref
variables.description: Planned elapsed time relative to the planned fixed reference value in CPTPTREF, represented in ISO 8601 duration format. Examples: "-PT15M" to represent 15 minutes prior to the reference time point indicated by CPTPTREF, "T8H" to represent 8 hours after the reference time point represented by CPTPTREF.

variables.name: CPTPTREF
variables.label: Time Point Reference
variables.description: Descriptive name of the fixed reference point referred to by CPTPT, CPTPTNUM, and CPELTM. Examples: "PREVIOUS DOSE", "PREVIOUS MEAL".

variables.name: CPRFTDTC
variables.label: Date/Time of Reference Time Point
variables.description: Date/time for a fixed reference time point defined by CPTPTREF.
